archetype.name: Pocket Passer (downfield)
archetype.definition: A rhythm thrower from the pocket who has stopped running, makes his living on throws 10+ yards down the field and over the middle, and takes the incompletions that come with that.

report.headline: A downfield passer carrying a dead run game, and finding his accuracy again
report.take:
Jordan Love's 2026 is two seasons stitched together. Through three weeks he was missing throws at a career-worst clip: a -9.7 CPOE against Minnesota while pressured on 47.8% of dropbacks, then -13.6 against the Jets and -8.5 against Atlanta. Over the last three games, all wins, his EPA per dropback is 0.279 and his CPOE is 5.2, which is last year's quarterback (5.5 CPOE, eighth in the league). His season-long 0.115 EPA per dropback (20th of 45) and -2.68 CPOE (35th) are mostly the hangover from that opening stretch.

The value comes from depth and the middle of the field. His throws of 10+ air yards are worth 0.461 EPA apiece and add up to 36.0 EPA, more than his whole dropback total of 27.9, because everything under 10 yards comes to only 9.2 and the behind-the-line stuff is negative. Deep balls land just 35.3% of the time but return 0.493 EPA a throw, and Christian Watson (0.504 EPA per target) is the reason. Over the middle he is at 0.498 EPA per attempt, while the right side barely clears average. A deep thrower should look like this: a low completion rate, a high payoff per throw.

The yardage hides how much of the offense he is carrying. Green Bay's run game is last in the league at -0.299 EPA per carry, and Love has gone from 13.3 rushing yards a game last year to 1.7, with a single scramble all season. That leaves him in long third downs, where he averages 7.9 yards to go, converts 33.3% and posts negative EPA. The line ranks 29th in hits allowed, and his time to throw has dropped to 2.57 seconds from 2.89. The 280.7 yards a game (fifth) owes as much to 37.7 attempts and two blowout losses as to efficiency.

His bad-throw rate of 15.5% looks alarming next to last year's 12.5%. His 2023 and 2024 seasons sat near 17%, though, so 2025's accuracy was his peak rather than his baseline. The likeliest version going forward is somewhere between the two halves of this season: a well-above-average downfield passer with a CPOE near zero, more volatile than his 2025 because he gets nothing from the run game.

strengths.title: Intermediate and deep throws pay
strengths.body: Throws beyond 10 air yards drive almost all of his value, and his 2.2 CPOE on deep balls means these are good throws, not just luck. This has been his profile for three seasons running, with aggressiveness steady around 15-17%. It should hold as long as Watson stays healthy.

strengths.title: Accuracy back over three games
strengths.body: Over the last three games his CPOE is 7.9 points above his season mark, and his EPA per dropback has more than doubled. The early slump came with heavy pressure and a brutal Minnesota defense, ranked first. The recent form looks closer to his 2025 self than a fluke, though Week 6 against the 31st-ranked Dallas defense came in at -5.8 CPOE.

strengths.title: Play-action from under center
strengths.body: Under center he is at 0.412 EPA per play with a 12.9 CPOE, against 0.043 and -7.3 from shotgun. The under-center sample is only 47 plays, so read it as a direction rather than a fact. It still says LaFleur's under-center looks give him clean, defined reads that the shotgun game hasn't.

concerns.title: Worst run game in football
concerns.body: Green Bay ranks 32nd in rushing EPA, which pushes Love into long-yardage passing downs. There he converts only a third of the time and posts negative EPA. This isn't his flaw, but it caps his efficiency and makes his good weeks more dependent on hitting downfield shots.

concerns.title: Accuracy slip and leaky protection
concerns.body: His bad-throw rate ranks 30th of 37 and his CPOE fell sharply from last year, while the line ranks 29th in hits allowed. His faster release reads as a response to that protection. His career says 2025's accuracy was the high-water mark, so expect something nearer his 2023-24 level.

concerns.title: Shaky in close fourth quarters
concerns.body: In one-score fourth quarters he is at -0.296 EPA per play with a -10.7 CPOE. That rests on just 20 plays, so it is more a hint than a trait. Still, it lines up with how hard third-and-long gets for this offense.

trend.note: Three bad-accuracy games to open, the worst against a top defense, then three wins at last year's efficiency. Week 5 against Chicago (16.9 EPA, 16.2 CPOE) was the peak, and Week 6 was solid but less precise.

nextGame.headline: Worst pass defense meets his downfield game, if protection holds
nextGame.body:
Detroit ranks last in defensive EPA and 28th against the pass. It gives up the most fantasy points and yards to quarterbacks, and its deep EPA allowed of 1.104 ranks 29th, which is exactly where Love does his damage. It is also the league's strongest pass funnel, so even a competent run game would get pushed toward the air, and Green Bay's run game isn't competent. Detroit's offense ranks third in EPA, and the Book has the game at 53.5 with the Lions favored by 3. That points to a shootout where Love keeps throwing all four quarters.

The catch is the rush: Detroit ranks sixth in hit rate and fourth in sack rate, against a Green Bay line that allows hits at a bottom-four clip. Guard Aaron Banks (toe) sat Week 6, and his listed return date is this game; a part-time starter coming back helps at the margins. On Detroit's side, safety Brian Branch (Achilles) is listed Out and corner Rock Ya-Sin (hamstring) questionable. A thinner back end would further help Love's throws over the middle and deep.

keyMatchups.title: Deep shots vs porous secondary
keyMatchups.body: Love's 10+ yard throws carry his season, and Detroit is among the worst defenses in the league against deep passes and explosive passes. If Branch is out, the middle of the field opens further for Watson and Golden.

keyMatchups.title: Lions pass rush vs weak line
keyMatchups.body: Detroit's sack rate ranks fourth, and Green Bay ranks 29th in hits allowed. Love's best games came when pressure was low, and his worst came at 47.8% pressured. This is the matchup that decides whether the shootout script delivers.

keyMatchups.title: Tucker Kraft vs soft TE coverage
keyMatchups.body: Detroit lets top tight ends score 8.5 PPR over their averages (31st) and sends an above-normal share of targets to tight ends. Kraft is Love's third option and a natural outlet against a blitz-heavy front.

nextGame.watch: Love's pressure rate: if the line keeps it near his season level, Detroit's secondary is there to be hit deep.

restOfSeason.body:
The volume is sustainable, and so is the downfield profile. The run game gives no sign of carrying more of the load, so Love should keep throwing 34-38 times a week, and his aggressiveness has held for three seasons. What should settle is the extremes. The early-season CPOE was too low for a quarterback who has never been that inaccurate across a full year. The last three games' 0.279 EPA per dropback is also hotter than a team with this protection and run game is likely to keep up. Expect efficiency in the top third of starters, with interceptions creeping toward his 2023-24 rate as the deep volume stays high.

Realistically that means about 250 to 295 passing yards a game with 1.5 to 2.1 touchdowns. Week-to-week swings will be wider than last year's, because so much of his value rides on a few explosive throws each game.
swingFactors: Whether the run game gets off the bottom of the league
Watson staying on the field as the deep target

confidence.note: Six starts, with a sharp early/late split; key splits (deep, under center) rest on under 50 plays.
